questions.q: How do representative superconducting and trapped-ion two-qubit gate speeds compare?
options: The two platforms have identical gate speeds in all published benchmarks

Superconducting gates are typically on the order of tens of nanoseconds, while trapped-ion gates are typically microseconds to a few hundred microseconds -- roughly two to three orders of magnitude slower
Gate speed cannot be compared across the two platforms because the concept of a 'gate' doesn't apply to trapped ions
Trapped-ion gates are consistently faster than superconducting gates
questions.explain: Trapped-ion gates depend on a slower mechanical process involving the chain's vibrational motion, making them commonly cited as roughly two to three orders of magnitude slower than superconducting gates, which are driven by fast microwave electronics.

questions.q: What does trapped-ion hardware trade to get all-to-all connectivity within a single chain, as covered across this chapter?
options: Trapped-ion qubits lose their ability to perform single-qubit gates once connectivity is enabled
All-to-all connectivity is only a marketing claim with no underlying physical basis
A chain can't grow indefinitely before motional-mode crowding degrades gate quality, requiring shuttling or photonic links between smaller chains to scale further
Nothing -- all-to-all connectivity has no associated cost or limit at any scale
questions.explain: All-to-all connectivity comes from ions sharing motional modes, but a longer chain's modes become too closely spaced to address cleanly -- so scaling past one chain reintroduces some routing-style overhead via shuttling or photonic interconnects (QCCD).

questions.q: How have reported two-qubit gate fidelities generally compared between the two platforms in recent published benchmarks?
options: Trapped-ion fidelities have generally trended somewhat higher than superconducting fidelities, though both have improved and the gap has narrowed, and specific figures should be treated as snapshots, not fixed specs
The two platforms use completely different definitions of fidelity that make any comparison meaningless
Superconducting fidelities have always been dramatically higher than trapped-ion fidelities with no exceptions
Fidelity has never been measured or reported for either platform
questions.explain: The lesson reports a general (hedged) trend of trapped-ion fidelities often being reported higher, while stressing that specific numbers from either camp are generation- and benchmark-specific snapshots, not permanent facts.

questions.q: Why are the two platforms' scalability bottlenecks described as 'genuinely different problems, not the same problem at different sizes'?
options: Scaling bottlenecks only apply to superconducting qubits, not trapped ions
Neither platform has any scaling bottleneck at all
Both platforms actually share the exact same scaling bottleneck, just described with different terminology

Superconducting scaling is limited by physical wiring density into the cryostat, while trapped-ion scaling is limited by laser-addressing precision and motional-mode crowding -- different engineering challenges entirely
questions.explain: Superconducting hardware's bottleneck is about control/readout wiring density into an extremely cold environment; trapped-ion hardware's bottleneck is about laser engineering and chain-length limits -- genuinely distinct problems that don't share solutions.

questions.q: What is the lesson's overall framing for comparing superconducting and trapped-ion hardware?
options: Neither platform wins across every dimension -- speed, connectivity, fidelity, scalability, and cost involve real, unresolved engineering tradeoffs rather than a settled winner
Trapped-ion hardware is strictly superior in every measurable respect
The comparison is purely a marketing exercise with no real technical differences between the platforms
Superconducting hardware is strictly superior in every measurable respect
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly argues against declaring either platform a winner, since each makes different, genuine tradeoffs across speed, connectivity, fidelity, scalability, and cost/footprint.
